facts.text: Founded in the mid‑19th century during westward expansion, Hampton was incorporated in 1896, laying out a modest grid for future growth.
The city took its name from Hampton Township.
The Minnesota & North Western Railway arrived in the late 1800s, linking Hampton to regional markets until the tracks were abandoned in 1984.
A one‑room schoolhouse once stood as a beacon of learning, where children from surrounding farms gathered to study reading, arithmetic, and history.
Hampton blends small‑town charm with steady growth, offering community events, local parks, and family‑owned businesses that welcome newcomers.
Early settlers, many of German descent, cleared the land, planted crops, and raised livestock, making agriculture more than an occupation—it was a way of life.
